title: Codimension-one criterion for open immersions between smooth trait models
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $F=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $X$ and $Z$ be smooth separated finite-type $T$-schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be open, containing $X_F$, and dense in both fibres of $X\to T$. Then $U$ contains every $x\in X$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\leq1$; here dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of prime ideals in the local ring. If $f:X\to Z$ is a $T$-morphism such that $f_F:X_F\to Z_F$ is an isomorphism and $f|_U:U\to Z$ is an open immersion, then $f$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: BLR 5.1 Theorem 5, proof of the no-shrinking assertion, printed p.114 (PDF p.120): codimension-one domain, differential determinant, and Zariski Main Theorem; the same argument applies to any morphism between smooth trait models; primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$. Every ideal of $R$ is principal, hence finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian; $T$ is Noetherian by the affine definition. The finite-type hypothesis makes $X$ Noetherian. A DVR has dimension one; since it is a local domain, its only primes are $(0)$ and $(\pi)$ (any intervening prime would give a chain of length two). Thus every nonempty open of $T$ contains its generic point $\eta$. Smoothness of $X\to T$ implies flatness and local finite presentation, and hence openness. For every nonempty open $W\subseteq X$, its image in $T$ is nonempty open and contains $\eta$, so $W\cap X_F\ne\varnothing$. In particular $X_F$ is dense in $X$, even when some fibres are empty.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (finite type over a Noetherian base), 01VF/01VE (smooth implies flat and lfp), 01UA (flat lfp open); algebra.tex Tag 00PD (DVR dimension). Density is the displayed elementary open-image argument.

proof.text: Let $x\in X$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\le1$. If $x$ lies over $\eta$, then $x\in X_F\subseteq U$. Otherwise $x$ lies over $(\pi)$. Apply the flat height formula to the Noetherian local rings $R\to A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, at the maximal prime of $A$: it gives $\dim A=1+\dim(A/\pi A)$. Thus $\dim(A/\pi A)=0$. This is the local ring of the special fibre at $x$. On an affine neighbourhood in that fibre, the prime corresponding to $x$ has no strictly smaller prime, by the localization correspondence and dimension zero. It is therefore a minimal prime, so $x$ is an irreducible-component generic point of the special fibre. The cited dense-fibre-open statement applies to the flat locally finitely presented morphism $X\to T$ and its dense open $U\cap X_s$, and puts $x$ in $U$. This proves the first assertion, including dimension-zero points.

source.place: Tag 00ON (dimension of flat base plus fibre), with morphisms.tex Tag 054U as in the dense-fibre-open node.

proof.text: Assume now that $f$ has the asserted properties. The universal derivations give $c:f^*\Omega^1_{Z/T}\to\Omega^1_{X/T}$, $a\otimes db\mapsto a\,d(f^\sharp b)$. Both modules are finite locally free: the differential sheaves are so by smoothness, and pulling back a local basis gives a local basis by the formula for module pullback. On $U$, the map $f$ identifies $U$ with an open subscheme of $Z$. Restriction of the affine differential construction to this open subscheme identifies the two differential modules and makes $c|_U$ an isomorphism. At any $x\in X$, choose an open neighbourhood $W$ on which both modules are free of finite constant ranks $r$ and $s$. If $W$ is nonempty, step 1 gives a point in $W\cap X_F\subseteq U$; tensoring the isomorphism there with its residue field shows $r=s$. Thus on $W$, $c$ is represented by a square matrix.

source.place: Tags 01UM (relative differential sheaf), 02G1 (smooth differentials finite locally free); equality of local ranks is finite-dimensional linear algebra at a point of U.

proof.text: Shrink $W$ to an affine neighbourhood of $x$ carrying these bases, and let $h$ be the determinant of the matrix. Its principal ideal defines a locally principal quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on $W$ (localize the principal ideal on basic affine opens). A matrix over a local ring is invertible precisely when its determinant is a unit, by the adjugate identity. Suppose $h$ is not a unit at $x$. Then $x$ lies in $V(h)$ and outside $U$, because $c|_U$ is invertible. By step 2 its stalk has dimension greater than one, in particular positive. The locally principal support lemma, applied on the locally Noetherian scheme $W$, gives a generalization $y\in V(h)\subseteq W$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{W,y}=1$. Open restriction identifies this local ring with $\mathcal O_{X,y}$. Step 2 gives $y\in U$, where $c$ and its determinant are invertible, contradicting $y\in V(h)$. Hence $h$ is a unit at every point, and $c$ is an isomorphism on every stalk. Rank zero causes no exception: the empty determinant is 1.

source.place: Tag 0BJG (lemma-find-point-codim-1), in its locally principal support form; determinant calculation is elementary.

proof.text: The new differential criterion applies with base $T$, source $X$, target $Z$, and the given $T$-morphism $f$: both structure maps are smooth, and step 4 proves the required stalk isomorphism at every point. It gives an open neighbourhood of every point on which $f$ is etale. Etaleness is local on the source, so $f$ is etale. In particular $f$ is smooth, hence flat and locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 02GU (Jacobian criterion); BLR 2.2 Corollary 10 is the precise relative differential criterion; Tags 02GJ (etale local on source), 02GK (etale implies smooth).

proof.text: Put $P=X\times_ZX$ and let $p_1:P\to X$ be the first projection. This is etale, being a base change of $f$. The diagonal $\Delta_f:X\to P$ is closed: its square with $\Delta_{X/T}:X\to X\times_TX$ and the natural map $P\to X\times_TX$ is Cartesian. Indeed, imposing equality of the two X-coordinates in P gives exactly X. Since $X\to T$ is separated, $\Delta_{X/T}$ is closed, and closed immersions remain closed under base change. Thus $f$ is separated by the diagonal definition. Separatedness is stable under base change, so $p_1$ is separated. Now $\Delta_f$ is a section of the etale separated morphism $p_1$. The section lemma identifies $X$ with an open and closed subscheme of $P$.

source.place: Tags 01JY/01QR (closed immersion base change), 01KU (separated base change), 01KT (section of separated morphism); etale.tex Tag 024T (section of unramified morphism).

proof.text: The generic fibre $P_F$ is dense in $P$. In fact, for every nonempty open $V\subseteq P$, the etale open-map property makes $p_1(V)$ a nonempty open of $X$. It meets $X_F$ by step 1, and a point in this intersection lifts to a point of $V\cap P_F$. The equality $P_F=(X_F)\times_{Z_F}(X_F)$ follows directly from the fibre-product universal property. Since $f_F$ is an isomorphism, the base change of $\Delta_f$ is an isomorphism onto $P_F$. Hence the open and closed image of $\Delta_f$ contains the dense subset $P_F$, so equals all of $P$. An open immersion onto the entire target is an isomorphism by its identification with an open subscheme. Consequently $\Delta_f$ is an isomorphism. This makes $f$ a monomorphism: any $a,b:H\to X$ with $fa=fb$ give $(a,b):H\to P$, which factors through the diagonal, implying $a=b$. Finally step 5 supplies flatness and local finite presentation, so the flat-lfp-monomorphism criterion makes $f$ an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 025G (flat locally finitely presented monomorphism is open immersion); morphisms.tex Tag 03WT (etale open map). Dense clopen diagonal argument replaces the final Zariski Main Theorem sentence of BLR 5.1 Theorem 5.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q48-6936b77b3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: I read the item and the one new node in full, plus every cited statement. All 7 steps are correct and every hypothesis is in force. (1) Spec R is Noetherian and has two points; smooth implies flat+lfp, so the map is open and X_F is dense in X. (2) The flat height formula (Stacks 00ON, read) gives dim A = 1 + dim A/πA. So a special-fibre point with dim ≤ 1 is a generic point of a component of the special fibre, and flat-fibre-dimension-strata-cover puts it in U. A dim-0 special-fibre point cannot exist. (3) c is an isomorphism on U, and the ranks are equal on a constant-rank neighbourhood because X_F is dense and lies in U. (4) A non-unit determinant at x forces dim O_x ≥ 2; locally-principal-support (Stacks pione 0BJG, read at pione.tex:4990) then gives a dim-1 generalization in V(h), which lies in U: contradiction. (5) The new criterion makes f étale, hence flat+lfp. (6) Δ_f is the base change of Δ_{X/T}, so f and p_1 are separated, and the section lemma makes Δ_f clopen. (7) P_F is dense because p_1 is open, so Δ_f is surjective and an isomorphism; f is a monomorphism, and flat-lfp-mono makes it an open immersion. The new node lem-sfb-smooth-morphism-cotangent-isomorphism-etale is true (BLR 2.2 Cor. 10 / EGA IV 17.11.2; checked on Frobenius, open immersions and mismatched ranks). It is statement-only and self-contained, it is not a clause of the item, and a DAG search found no duplicate (it differs from smooth-zero-differentials-affine-open-etale, pur-etale-at-point-from-differentials, a1-nonzero-differential-generically-etale, etale-localization-relative-differentials and trf-cotangent-isomorphism-coordinate-lift).
